chapterTitle: Unit 08: Projection of a Side of a Triangle
subject: math-10

questions.question: In an obtuse-angled triangle, the square on the side opposite to the obtuse angle is equal to the sum of the squares on the sides containing the obtuse angle together with:

options.A: Twice the rectangle contained by one of those sides and the projection of the other upon it
options.B: The rectangle contained by one of those sides and the projection
options.C: Twice the square of the median
options.D: Half the product of the two sides

questions.explanation: Theorem 1 of Unit 8 states: c² = a² + b² + 2ap (for obtuse angle opposite side c).

questions.question: In an acute-angled triangle, the square on the side opposite to an acute angle is equal to the sum of the squares on the sides containing that acute angle:

options.A: Diminished by twice the rectangle contained by one of those sides and the projection of the other upon it
options.B: Increased by twice the rectangle contained by those sides
options.D: Equal to the sum of their squares only

questions.explanation: Theorem 2 states: c² = a² + b² - 2ap for an acute angle.

questions.question: When the included angle of a triangle becomes a right angle (90°), the projection p becomes zero, and the theorem reduces to:
questions.explanation: With angle = 90°, p = 0, leaving c² = a² + b², which is Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.question: Apollonius' theorem relates the sides of any triangle to its:
questions.explanation: Apollonius' Theorem states: AB² + AC² = 2(AD² + BD²), where AD is the median to side BC.

questions.question: The geometric projection of a point upon a straight line is a:
questions.explanation: Projecting a point P onto line L produces the single point where the perpendicular from P intersects L.

questions.question: The projection of a line segment perpendicular to a given line upon that line is a:
questions.explanation: If a segment is perpendicular to the line of projection, both its endpoints project onto the exact same point, so its projection length is zero.

questions.question: The projection of a line segment parallel to a given line upon that line has length:

options.A: Equal to the length of the segment

questions.explanation: When a segment is parallel to the target line, the projected segment forms an exact rectangle with it, preserving its original length.

In triangle ABC with obtuse angle C, if a = 4, b = 3, and projection p = 1, then c² is:
In triangle ABC, if c² > a² + b², then angle C is:
questions.explanation: If c² > a² + b², the opposite angle C is obtuse (> 90°).

questions.question: In triangle ABC, if c² < a² + b², then angle C is:
questions.explanation: If the square on the longest side is less than the sum of the squares on the other two, all angles are acute (< 90°).

questions.question: In triangle ABC, if c² = a² + b², then angle C is:
questions.explanation: By the Converse of Pythagoras' Theorem, c² = a² + b² implies angle C = 90°.

questions.question: If the sides of a triangle are 6 cm, 8 cm, and 10 cm, the triangle is:
questions.explanation: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10². Hence it is a right-angled triangle.

questions.question: If the sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 7 cm, and 9 cm, the triangle is:
questions.explanation: 5² + 7² = 25 + 49 = 74. Since 9² = 81 > 74, the triangle is obtuse-angled.

questions.question: If the sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 6 cm, and 7 cm, the triangle is:
questions.explanation: 5² + 6² = 25 + 36 = 61. Since 7² = 49 < 61, the triangle is acute-angled.

questions.question: In Apollonius' theorem, if D is the midpoint of BC, the median AD divides BC into two segments such that BD = :
questions.explanation: By definition of midpoint, D bisects BC into BD = CD = BC/2.

questions.question: The projection of side AC on side BC of triangle ABC is denoted mathematically by:

options.A: The segment between the foot of perpendicular from A and vertex C

questions.explanation: Projection of AC on BC is the segment CD where D is the foot of the perpendicular dropped from A to line BC.

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle of side 's', the length of the projection of any side on another side is:
questions.explanation: Projection = s · cos 60° = s(1/2) = s/2.

questions.question: If a line segment makes an angle θ with a line L, the length of its projection on L is:
questions.explanation: By trigonometry, adjacent side in the right projection triangle is Hypotenuse · cos θ.

questions.question: In any parallelogram, the sum of the squares on the four sides is equal to the:

options.A: Sum of the squares on its diagonals
options.C: Twice the sum of its diagonals

questions.explanation: The Parallelogram Law (derived from Apollonius' Theorem) states 2(a² + b²) = d₁² + d₂².
